name: Popover
summary: A small surface anchored to its trigger for one or two controls or a short explanation — adjust the weekly target, edit a priority, 'what counts as a quality application'. Non-blocking in look, modal for assistive technology by default (the page is hidden and focus is contained, as in Menu); isNonModal exists for combobox-style surfaces only. Not for a decision (Modal), not for a list of actions (Menu), not for a one-line hint on hover (Tooltip).

pattern.name: Dialog (non-modal popover) — APG dialog pattern in a positioned overlay

trigger.intent: The Button it is anchored to. DialogTrigger wires aria-expanded and aria-controls and restores focus on close. React Aria does not emit aria-haspopup for dialogs — the name of the popover, read on open, tells the user what it is.

title.requiredWhen: aria-label is not given. Rendered as a small heading (Heading slot="title", h3) and read first.
title.intent: The accessible name AND the visible heading: 'Weekly target'.

aria-label.requiredWhen: title is omitted — a popover that is a single control with its own label.

children.intent: At most a couple of controls and a sentence. The function form receives close() so a Done button can dismiss. More than that is a Modal.

placement.intent: Preferred side and alignment; flips when there is no room. Gap to the trigger is space.200 (8 px), read from the token at runtime — React Aria positions with a number.

onOpenChange.intent: Closed by any means: Escape, close(), a click outside (modal) or focus leaving (non-modal).

isNonModal.intent: false (default): the page is hidden from assistive technology, scroll is locked, Tab is contained, a click outside closes — React Aria's default, safe for screen readers. true: the page stays reachable and the popover closes when focus leaves it. React Aria warns this degrades the screen-reader experience; use it only for a combobox-style surface, never for a form.

isKeyboardDismissDisabled.intent: Escape always closes unless set. Set only when Escape would lose typed input — then a Done/Cancel control must be inside.

showArrow.intent: A decorative arrow pointing at the trigger (OverlayArrow). Visual only; it carries no meaning and no colour of its own.

size.intent: Max width 320 / 400 px (8 / 10 × size.target.lg). A popover wider than that is a Modal.

padding.intent: Inset 8 / 16 px (space.inset.sm / md). sm for a single control.

keyboard.action: Opens. Focus moves to the first focusable control inside, or to the popover itself if there is none.
Default (modal for AT): cycle inside only — contained, as in Menu (ADR-029). isNonModal: focus leaves and the popover closes.
Closes and returns focus to the trigger (unless isKeyboardDismissDisabled).
Closes (modal: interact-outside; non-modal: the blur does it) and returns focus to the trigger.

a11y.name: From title (a heading wired by aria-labelledby) or aria-label — the type union requires one of the two.
a11y.announcements: role="dialog"; the trigger gets aria-expanded and aria-controls (React Aria emits no aria-haspopup for dialogs). Default mode hides everything outside with aria-hidden (React Aria ariaHideOutside) and locks scroll; both are undone on close. React Aria omits aria-modal (inconsistent AT support) — the same as Modal.
a11y.targetSize: Not a target itself. The trigger is a Button; controls inside are system components and meet their own sizes.

rules: One or two controls, or a sentence. If it needs a footer with Cancel and a primary, it is a Modal. If it is a list of actions, it is a Menu. If it is a one-line hint, it is a Tooltip.

Modal for assistive technology by default (Menu precedent, ADR-029): the page is hidden, scroll locked, Tab contained, a click outside closes. isNonModal is the exception for combobox-style surfaces and is never used for a form — React Aria's own warning.
Focus moves in on open — the first control, or the popover itself — and returns to the trigger on close (2.4.3). The popover element shows the inset ring when it holds focus itself.
The title is a real heading (h3, Heading slot="title") and the first thing read; without one, aria-label. Never an unlabelled dialog.
The gap to the trigger is space.200, read from the token at runtime because React Aria positions with a number. This is the one place a token value crosses into JavaScript; it is read, never typed.
Never nest popovers, and never open a Menu from inside one. One overlay at a time.
The body uses Card-raised tokens plus shadow.overlay (dark themes drop the shadow through the token); it is not a Card, because a popover's inset is 8 / 16 px.
The arrow is decorative: optional, no meaning, no separate colour (it is the surface and border, rotated). No z-index token yet (PARKING.md); the portal's DOM order stacks it above Toast.

properties.Placement: placement (top / bottom / start / end × start / end alignment)
properties.Title: title

examples.title: Adjust the weekly target
examples.code: <Popover trigger={<Button variant="tertiary">Adjust</Button>} title="Weekly target" placement="bottom end">{(close) => (<><TextField label="Applications per week" inputMode="numeric" defaultValue="5" /><Button variant="primary" onPress={close}>Done</Button></>)}</Popover>

examples.title: A short explanation
examples.code: <Popover trigger={<Button variant="tertiary" aria-label="What counts?" iconStart={<InfoIcon />} />} title="What counts as quality" showArrow>Fit ≥ 70, or an application you marked Stretch on purpose.</Popover>

examples.title: Combobox-style surface (non-modal)
examples.code: <Popover trigger={<Button>Filter…</Button>} aria-label="Filter leads" isNonModal size="md"><TextField aria-label="Search filters" /></Popover>
